summary.title: Diffusion Models from Scratch
summary.one_liner: You learn the core mechanics of diffusion models by building a toy noise-corruption process, a minimal UNet, a training loop and iterative sampling on MNIST, then compare it to the diffusers DDPM UNet2DModel.
keywords: how do diffusion models generate images
elucidating the design space of diffusion-based generative models
takeaways: Noise corruption can be done by mixing an image with random noise by an amount, keeping values in range.
A minimal UNet with down path, up path and skip connections can predict the clean image from a noisy input.
Training uses random noise amounts and MSE loss between the model's prediction and the clean image.
Sampling starts from random noise and repeatedly moves a fraction of the way toward the model's prediction.
The diffusers DDPM version differs by predicting noise, using timestep conditioning, a richer UNet and a noise schedule.
summary.summary: This Hugging Face Diffusion Course notebook builds a toy diffusion model in PyTorch on MNIST. It implements a simple corruption function that mixes images with noise, a minimal BasicUNet with skip connections, a training loop using MSE loss, and an iterative sampling procedure. It then compares this to the diffusers UNet2DModel and DDPM approach, covering the noise schedule, noise-prediction objective, timestep conditioning and alternative samplers. The page is code-heavy and explicitly illustrative rather than production code.
